extracted.subtask_description: Form paragraphs and substantive criteria for making rejections under 35 U.S.C. 101 and 112 (utility, written description, enablement, indefiniteness, new matter, duplicate claims, etc.) in U.S. patent prosecution. Guidance is for examiners preparing Office actions and for practitioners responding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimed subject matter must fall within one of the four categories recited in 35 U.S.C. 101: process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claim is directed to a judicial exception (abstract idea, natural phenomenon, law of nature), explain why it is a judicial exception and whether the claim is directed to a practical application of that exception (e.g., requires physical transformation or produces a useful, concrete, and tangible result). Also explain if the claim would impermissibly preempt all substantial practical applications of the exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility requirement (35 U.S.C. 101) — Utility Lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: The claimed invention lacks patentable utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must provide explanation of lack of utility (see MPEP §§ 706.03(a) and 2105-2107.03). Use form paragraph for this rejection and identify facts supporting absence of a credible/specific/substantial utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inoperative invention — lacks utility
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosed invention is inoperative and therefore lacks utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must explain why the invention is inoperative when asserting lack of utility (use corresponding form paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility must be specific/substantial/credible or well-established
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be supported by either an asserted utility that is specific and substantial (or credible) or by a well-established utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Format A when there is no asserted utility or asserted utility is not specific and substantial; Format B when utility must be characterized as 'credible'; Format C when multiple utilities exist with varying sufficiency — address each utility. When lacking, also make a 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph (enablement) rejection as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Energy Act restrictions (statutory bar and handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent shall be granted for inventions useful solely in utilization of special nuclear material or atomic energy in an atomic weapon; applications disclosing or appearing to disclose atomic-energy-related inventions are reported to the Department of Energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications relating to atomic energy are screened by TC work group 3640; rejections based on sections 151(a), 152, or 155 of the Atomic Energy Act must be made only by TC work group 3640 personnel. Reporting to DOE does not itself determine patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description requirement (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain a written description of the invention and the manner and process of making and using it in full, clear, concise, and exact terms to enable one skilled in the art to make and use the invention; must set forth the best mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.30.01 (statutory quotation) must precede many 112 first-paragraph rejections in first actions on the merits and final rejections. Cite relevant MPEP sections and use this paragraph ONCE in a given Office action where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description deficiency (claim contains subject matter not described)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, for failing to comply with the written description requirement because the claim contains subject matter not described in the specification so as to reasonably convey possession to one skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify by page/line and/or figure the subject matter not properly described and explain the position, including any unanswered examiner questions that raise doubt about possession at filing. This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.01 (or 7.103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, when the specification does not enable one skilled in the art to make and/or use the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify claimed subject matter for which the specification is not enabling and explain why, applying the In re Wands factors (and undue experimentation analysis) as appropriate (see In re Wands, 858 F.2d 731). Precede with form paragraph 7.30.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of enablement must be commensurate with claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When the specification is enabling for some embodiments but the claims are broader, the claims may be rejected because the specification does not provide enablement commensurate in scope with the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.31.03 when scope of claims exceeds scope of enabling disclosure. Identify the enabling portions of the specification and the claim aspects that are not enabled; explain using In re Wands factors and cite MPEP §§ 2164.01(a) and 2164.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, when the best mode contemplated by the inventor has not been disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State basis for holding that best mode has been concealed (e.g., quality of disclosure effectively conceals best mode). Use this form paragraph rarely and precede with form paragraph 7.30.01. See MPEP §§ 2165-2165.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential subject matter missing from claims (enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject when a feature considered critical or essential by applicant to practice the claimed invention is omitted from the claims and the disclosure does not enable practice without it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recite the omitted subject matter and give rationale for considering it critical or essential, citing applicant statements/arguments/drawings/etc. that demonstrate applicant viewed the feature as essential. Precede with form paragraph 7.30.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph — claims must particularly point out and distinctly claim
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must conclude with one or more claims particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter regarded as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.30.02 quotes the statute and must precede rejections based on the 2nd paragraph (used once per Office action as required). See MPEP §§ 2171-2174 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to claim applicant's invention (claims inconsistent with applicant statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, for failing to set forth the subject matter which applicant regards as their invention — based on applicant submissions outside the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the applicant paper (date) where applicant stated a different invention and explain how that statement indicates a different invention from what is claimed. Precede with form paragraph 7.30.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefiniteness — failure to particularly point out and distinctly claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected as indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify particular term(s) or limitation(s) rendering claim indefinite and explain why. If claim scope can be determined by one of ordinary skill, a rejection is not appropriate. Precede with form paragraph 7.30.02 (or 7.103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim term used inconsistently with accepted meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant acts as their own lexicographer to give a claim term a meaning contrary to its ordinary meaning, the written description must clearly redefine the term and set forth the uncommon definition to put one skilled in the art on notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the term, the meaning assigned in the claim, and the accepted meaning, with support for the accepted meaning (textbook/dictionary). This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative term / term of degree renders claim indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative term (term of degree) that is not defined by the claim or the specification and for which no standard for ascertaining the requisite degree is provided renders the claim indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain which parameter/quantity/limitation is made indefinite by the term and how the specification fails to provide a standard. Precede with form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad range and narrow range in same claim renders claim indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad range or limitation together with a narrow range or limitation that falls within the broad range (in the same claim) is considered indefinite because it raises doubt whether the narrower language is exemplary or required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the broader and narrower ranges and locations in the claim; modify to fit other instances of indefiniteness. Precede with form paragraph 7.34.01. See Ex parte Wu and MPEP § 2173.05(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of antecedent basis in the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim recites a limitation without sufficient antecedent basis (e.g., 'said lever' or 'the lever' without prior introduction), making scope indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the limitation lacking antecedent basis and where it appears in the claim. Use this paragraph only in aggravated situations where scope is indeterminate. Precede with form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claims must recite steps — mere 'use' may be indefinite/improper
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim that provides for the use of something but does not set forth any steps involved in the method/process is unclear what method/process is intended and is indefinite; a mere recitation of a use may also be an improper process claim under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert what is being used and, if applicable, reference related claims. This paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01. See MPEP § 2173.05(q) and cited cases for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims are literal translations — narrative/grammatical defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims appearing to be literal translations into English from a foreign document that are narrative and replete with grammatical/idiomatic errors are generally indefinite and fail to conform to U.S. practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph (preceded by 7.34.01) to describe failure to conform to claim drafting norms and indicate need for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite claim language: 'for example', 'such as', 'or the like'
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases like 'for example', 'such as', or 'or the like' render claims indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following those phrases are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific form paragraph for the offending phrase (7.34.08 for 'for example', 7.34.10 for 'such as', 7.34.09 for 'or the like'). These must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01 and reference MPEP § 2173.05(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function modifier lacks specified function (35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where 'means' is used but the word(s) preceding 'means' do not convey a function, it is impossible to determine equivalents as required by 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, and the claim is indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure words preceding 'means' convey a function (e.g., 'latch means' conveys 'latching'). If not, the claim is indefinite. Precede with form paragraph 7.34.01 and cite Ex parte Klumb.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential steps omitted from method claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph when essential steps are omitted, creating a gap between steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the omitted steps and give rationale for considering them critical or essential. This paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential elements omitted from claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph for omitting essential elements such that the claim is incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recite the omitted elements and give rationale for considering them critical or essential. Precede with form paragraph 7.30.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential structural cooperative relationships omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph when essential cooperative structural relationships among elements are omitted, creating a gap between necessary structural connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recite omitted structural cooperative relationships and explain why they are critical. Precede with form paragraph 7.30.02. See MPEP § 2172.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro se claim drafting deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro se claims may be narrative, indefinite, and contain functional/operational language; device structure must be clearly and positively specified and claims must be in one-sentence form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.34.15 for pro se applicants and note the format of claims in cited patents as examples. Precede with form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omnibus claim — 'substantially as shown and described' is indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: An omnibus-style claim (e.g., 'A device substantially as shown and described') is indefinite for failing to point out what is included or excluded by the claim language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.35 for omnibus claims; this must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02. No further explanation is necessary for such a rejection; see MPEP § 1302.04(b) for cancellation upon allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark or trade name used as claim limitation is indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark or trade name used in a claim to identify or describe a material/product does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph because a trademark identifies source, not the goods, making claim scope uncertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the trademark/trade name and what it is used to identify/describe; specify the material/product and explain why identification/description is indefinite. Precede with form paragraph 7.30.02 and cite Ex parte Simpson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate claims — substantial duplicates objection/warning (37 CFR 1.75)
rubrics_metrics.description: When two claims are duplicates or so close in content that they cover the same thing, after allowing one claim the other can be objected to under 37 CFR 1.75 as a substantial duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.05.05 to warn applicant and 7.05.06 to object when claims are duplicates. If duplicate claims are allowable, use 7.05.06; otherwise use 7.05.05 to give applicant opportunity to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibited (35 U.S.C. 132(a)) — objection to added material
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention. Adding subject matter not disclosed in the original application (including specific percentages/compounds after a broader disclosure or omission of a step) is new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Object to new matter using form paragraph 7.28, identify added material by page/line or figure, provide explanation and unresolved questions, and require cancellation of the new matter in reply. If new matter affects claims, make corresponding 35 U.S.C. 112 first-paragraph rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filing without license — abandonment and statutory consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an application in a foreign country prior to six months after filing in the United States without authorization may constitute abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 182 and related statutes, and may result in forfeiture of claims against the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants subject to orders under section 181 must obtain a license to file abroad; the Commissioner may treat unauthorized foreign filing as abandonment as of the time of violation. Licenses may be granted retroactively in narrow circumstances (error without deceptive intent and non-disclosing of section 181 subject matter).
